title: Read-only audit of the agent harness, instruction precedence, memory, skills, tools, and decoding-pipeline leakage safety, per Sol's Handout 1 -- ahead of adding structured (unit x time / channel x time) omission-identity decoding

preflight.drift_note: assumed baseline branch no longer exists (merged into dev earlier the same day as this audit); the assumed 'known dirty file' is now committed and clean. Re-verified live per the handout's own instruction not to assume the state is unchanged.

claims.statement: The retracted O+ census figure (421/8597 = 4.90%, CONTEXT.md §8 marks it 'Synthetic') is live and unlabeled in two pieces of executable code, not just prose: notebooks/reproducibility_master_pipeline.py and its paired .ipynb hard-assert tot==8597 and o==421 and print 'PASS: inclusive O+ = 4.90%' as if it were a verified reproducibility check; jnwb/unit_classification.py:539 states the figure as current fact in a live, imported library docstring.
claims.receipt: notebooks/reproducibility_master_pipeline.py lines 6,44-46 and paired .ipynb cells 23,27 (assert + print PASS). jnwb/unit_classification.py:539. Referenced, not archived: README.md:116 lists the notebook suite. CONTEXT.md:203 marks the same number 'Synthetic'; CLAUDE.md:206 calls it 'a retracted 421'.

claims.statement: The Labyrinth graph schema supports supersession (supersedes/contradicts/corrects edge relations, all in real use across 378 nodes) but does not enforce it onto the target node's own status field -- a node can be the explicit target of a contradicts edge and still read status:confirmed, issues:[] indefinitely. Of 378 nodes, status values observed are confirmed(354)/null(13)/provisional(3)/unconfirmed(3)/resolved(1)/open(1) -- zero use 'retracted'.
claims.receipt: artifacts/.lab/census_provenance_synthetic_finding_20260728.json (status confirmed, severity critical) contains an edge to analysis-clopper-pearson-confidence-intervals with relation contradicts and an explicit unactioned note 'It should be demoted.' Three sibling nodes still read status:confirmed, issues:[] and still assert 421/8597=4.90% as fact: artifacts/.lab/analysis-hierarchical-inference-mixed-effects.json, artifacts/.lab/analysis-exploratory-vs-headline-evidence-hierarchy.json, artifacts/.lab/analysis-clopper-pearson-confidence-intervals.json.

claims.statement: 11 of 14 decoding scripts in scripts/ use invalid random/ungrouped cross-validation (StratifiedKFold(shuffle=True) or train_test_split(stratify=y,...) with no groups= parameter anywhere) for omission-identity-style inference, exactly the confound the project's own doctrine already names as invalid. Two of the eleven additionally fit StandardScaler on the full dataset before cross_val_score, classic pre-split leakage. None of the 11 are archived (no archive_oneoff/ prefix) or inline-flagged as historical/invalid -- filenames alone (v4...v9) give no signal.
claims.receipt: Invalid (11): decode_fig04_v4_area_ranking.py, decode_fig04_v5_NxT_pca_svm.py, decode_fig04_v6_2d_population_5windows.py, decode_fig04_v7_bilinear_5windows.py, decode_fig04_v8_permutation_null.py, decode_fig04_v9_nam.py, decode_splus_pfc_single_session_step1.py, decode_splus_pfc_single_session_step2.py, decode_splus_pfc_single_session_step12_balanced.py, decode_lfp_1d_positive_control_and_omission.py, compute_omission_identity_encoding.py. Pre-split scaler leakage: compute_omission_identity_encoding.py:115,136 (scaler.fit_transform(X) / X_all before cross_val_score) and compute_omission_identity_encoding_v2.py:325 (X_s = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X) before cross_val_score line 326). Valid (2 of 14, for comparison): scripts/compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py (grouped leave-one-cycle-out, in-fold balancing/scaling, exchangeable within-cycle permutation null); jnwb/omission_identity.py's decode_identity_cycle_deconfound used by compute_omission_identity_cycle_deconfound_v3.py (grouped LOCO for the observed statistic).
claims.note: This directly and concretely explains the mechanism behind the already-known-confounded 0.601 random-CV accuracy figure cited throughout CONTEXT.md/REVISION_PLAN.md/FIGURE_SUMMARY.md doctrine -- this claim supplies the code-level receipt for a fact the project already believed.

claims.statement: jnwb/omission_identity.py's decode_identity_cycle_deconfound (used by compute_omission_identity_cycle_deconfound_v3.py, the source of the ~0.495 chance-compatible headline result) correctly uses leave-one-cycle-out CV for its OBSERVED A-vs-B accuracy, but its permutation NULL uses a naive global label permutation across all trials that ignores cycle membership entirely -- unlike the newer compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py, which correctly preserves per-cycle class counts via _within_cycle_permutation. This is an asymmetry between how the observed statistic and its null are computed.
claims.receipt: jnwb/omission_identity.py:551-554 (rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state); for _ in range(n_permutations): y_perm = rng.permutation(yab) -- global, not grouped by cyc_ab). Compare compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py:122-130 (_within_cycle_permutation, loops np.unique(cycles) and permutes within each group only).
claims.note: Direction of bias not proven here -- does not obviously overturn the chance-compatible conclusion, but must be fixed before this specific null is used to support any future POSITIVE claim, and should not be assumed safe in either direction without checking.

claims.statement: Two of the most consequential documented doctrines in this project are present in CLAUDE.md/other skills but ABSENT from the exact skills an agent would consult to apply them: (1) TFR ratio-before-log10/dB averaging order is stated once, in match-my-writing-style (a prose-style skill), and is completely absent from jnwb-tfr and jnwb-visualization, the two skills that actually compute/plot dB TFR values. (2) CV/permutation exchangeability-and-grouping is well-covered in jnwb-functional-connectivity and nwb-analysis-forms, but absent from jnwb-statistics.permutation_test and jnwb-jrsa's generic jrsa(permutations=...) API -- exactly the two generic entry points most likely to be misused with a naive per-sample permutation on this session/cycle-structured corpus.
claims.receipt: jnwb-tfr/SKILL.md and jnwb-visualization/SKILL.md (both .claude and .agents copies) grepped for averaging-order language: no match. match-my-writing-style/SKILL.md line ~205-207 has the rule. jnwb-statistics/SKILL.md's permutation_test description (lines ~103-109) and jnwb-jrsa/SKILL.md's jrsa(...permutations=1000...) description (line ~14) both grepped for grouping/exchangeability language: no match in either. jnwb-functional-connectivity/SKILL.md lines 39-49 has the correct within-session design as contrast.
claims.note: This is a root-cause finding, not just a gap: it directly explains how the plot_tfr dB-averaging bug (jnwb/session.py, found and fixed earlier the same day, see session-py-tfr-plot-baseline-bugs-20260810.json) went unnoticed, and how the naive-global-permutation bug in claim-p0-deconfound-null-ignores-cycle-grouping could exist uncaught. Closing this gap in Handout 2's skill patch would plausibly have prevented both.

claims.statement: The .claude/ directory -- which AGENTS.md itself declares is 'the location Claude Code's project-skill loader actually reads' -- is entirely gitignored, making it untracked, invisible to git history, and not guaranteed present in a fresh clone. The .gitignore line that appears to carve out an exception for one file is syntactically inert (tab-separated trailing text on a single pattern line, not a second pattern), so it has no effect.
claims.receipt: .gitignore:112 = '.claude/\t.claude/skills/labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md' (tab-separated, one .gitignore pattern per line is the actual syntax, so everything after the first token is inert). git ls-files .claude returns nothing. git check-ignore -v .claude/skills/labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md confirms exclusion by that exact line despite the file being named in the trailing text.

claims.statement: The two skill trees (.agents/skills/, tracked, called 'reference-only' by AGENTS.md; .claude/skills/, gitignored, called 'authoritative for loading') have already drifted substantially. diff on labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md alone shows 348 of ~450 combined lines differ. Only jnwb-jrsa and match-my-writing-style are byte-identical between the two trees; every other pair differs in line count.
claims.receipt: diff .agents/skills/labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md .claude/skills/labyrinth-protocol/SKILL.md -> 348 differing lines (9,978 bytes/Aug 4 vs 12,043 bytes/Aug 8). jnwb-core: 267 lines (.claude) vs 192 (.agents). jnwb-tfr: 193 vs 179. jnwb-visualization: 297 vs 273. A scripts/sync_claude_skills.py exists but its actual run cadence could not be confirmed from static inspection; the observed drift suggests it either wasn't run recently or doesn't fully reconcile content.

claims.statement: pyproject.toml (name='omission', packages=['jnwb']) and a second, vestigial setup.py at repo root (name='pypeline', entry_points console_scripts pypeline=pypeline.core:cli, deps include torch/kilosort but omit scipy/scikit-learn/matplotlib/statsmodels that pyproject.toml declares required) define two different, conflicting packages for the same repository.
claims.receipt: pyproject.toml [project] name='omission', [tool.setuptools] packages=['jnwb']. setup.py name='pypeline', entry_points={'console_scripts':['pypeline=pypeline.core:cli']}, narrower/different install_requires.

Looks like a copy-paste error. CONTEXT.md §10 still lists this file as a live source for intro/discussion/abstract voice, i.e. not archived/historical.
claims.receipt: context/drafts/04_draft_biorxiv_markdown.md:118 vs :122. .agents/skills/jnwb-core/SKILL.md:68 and match-my-writing-style/SKILL.md:172-174 correctly define AAAB as structured ('All A's, B deviant'). Current working draft context/drafts/omission-a-draft-v3.md checked directly: no such mislabeling found.

claims.statement: context/figures/INVENTORY.md (auto-generated; header says 'do not hand-edit, re-run the script instead') still carries a fig04 section heading reading 'currently 100% synthetic, not yet a real result.' This predates the 2026-08-06/08-08 evolution in which _v2 tables now exist (a confounded, non-zero result, not an absence of data) -- the heading is stale relative to CONTEXT.md §12A's more current framing, and nothing triggered regeneration after the underlying figure state changed.
claims.receipt: context/figures/INVENTORY.md:48. Compare context/docs/CONTEXT.md §12A (2026-08-08 audit) and context/figures/fig04_omission_identity_decoding/README.md:32, both current and correctly framing the state as confounded-diagnostic-only, not absent.

claims.statement: Trial tables preserve the full condition string (e.g. 'AXAB') and cycle_id, and session/subject are tracked at the outer loop level, but preceding_identity, sequence_family, and omission_position are not materialized as explicit, reusable trial-table columns. They have been re-derived ad hoc three separate times already: the v2 block-number confound diagnosis, the v3 cycle-detection fix, and the Aug-6 p4 condition-label swap fix.
claims.receipt: scripts/compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py's _trial_table() (lines 298-320): columns are start_time, label, label_int, condition, condition_trial_index, cycle_id, fold, trial_index -- no explicit preceding_identity/sequence_family/omission_position columns. jnwb/omission_identity.py:37-44 (p4 label-swap fix, self-documented: 'Every p4-specific number computed before this fix... must be treated as unreliable until rerun').

claims.statement: No skill anywhere in the repo addresses the fact that SPK unit ordering (row position in session.get_units(area)) has no biological topology, unlike LFP channel ordering along a laminar probe. This is exactly the concern Sol's handout raises about a future unit x time CNN treating unit-index adjacency as meaningful, and it is currently unaddressed by any doctrine source.
claims.receipt: compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py itself already flags this implicitly in its own output metadata: cell['unit_identity'] = 'session.get_units(area).index row position' (line 481) -- an honest label, but not a warning against convolving across that axis. No hit for 'unit order'/'unit topology'/'unit adjacency' in any skill file.

claims.statement: Collected lower-severity tooling/consistency gaps, none blocking: (1) session-count 'do not hardcode' warning is inconsistently extended across skills (present in jnwb-core/jnwb-metadata, absent from jnwb-population's unit counts); (2) session Python 3.14.3 vs CI-tested 3.11 only, no upper bound in pyproject.toml, though test collection is clean; (3) no shared numpy-safe JSON encoder, manual per-callsite casting only; (4) mixed legacy np.random.seed(42) vs modern default_rng pattern across the codebase; (5) no schema validator for artifacts/.lab/*.json nodes -- schema_version stamped on write, never asserted on read; (6) the POSIX-path-for-HDF5-internals lesson is correctly applied in jnwb/compression.py but not written into CLAUDE.md or any skill.
claims.receipt: Full detail in docs/agent_harness_audit_20260810.md Section E table and the underlying research-agent transcripts (tools-friction pass).

claims.statement: Swept the full repo for a hardcoded minimum-training-accuracy acceptance criterion (patterns: train(ing)?_?(accuracy|acc)\s*(must|should|>=|>), minimum accuracy, accuracy threshold). Zero matches in project code; one unrelated match inside the vendored sklearn library. Clean -- no such rule exists to remove before structured decoding begins.
claims.receipt: grep -rniE across the repo, excluding .venv, for the three patterns Sol's handout section I specifies: only hit is .venv/Lib/site-packages/sklearn/metrics/_ranking.py (an sklearn docstring example, not project code).

claims.statement: Of the falsification controls Sol's handout Section J requires, label permutation and cycle-aware label permutation have working precedent (compute_omission_identity_leakage_safe.py). Structured-vs-flattened comparison, unit-order permutation, channel-order permutation, time-bin permutation, within-trial temporal scrambling, capacity-matched MLP control, and the presented-identity positive control have no existing implementation anywhere in the repo -- all would be new code required by the proposed structured-decoding skill.
claims.receipt: Grepped scripts/ and jnwb/ for permutation-control patterns beyond label permutation: no unit-order/channel-order/time-bin permutation implementation found; no capacity-matched-MLP-control pattern found; no presented-identity positive-control decode script found (the closest is the general presented-stimulus decoding referenced in nwb-analysis-forms/SKILL.md §7, not yet run as a formal positive control receipt).

issues: This audit is read-only per its mandate -- none of the P0/P1 findings above have been fixed yet, except the plot_tfr dB bug which was found and fixed earlier the same day as an unrelated task and is only cross-referenced here.

The 11 invalid-CV decode scripts should be archived (moved to scripts/archive_oneoff/ with a header note) or given an inline deprecation header, NOT deleted -- Conservation applies. Deleting would lose the record of what was tried and why it was superseded.

Sections A-E were produced by four parallel background research agents; Sections F-J and the decode-script leakage sweep were done by direct file reads by the compiling agent, specifically because leakage/confound judgment calls should not be delegated blind. Cross-validation between the two: the skills-audit agent's finding that jnwb-tfr/jnwb-statistics lack the log-order/grouping rules independently corroborates the compiling agent's direct-code finding of the plot_tfr bug and the deconfound-null asymmetry -- two independent methods converged on the same root cause.

verdict.SAFE_TO_PATCH_AGENT_conditions: Patch (Handout 2) should incorporate: unit-order-has-no-topology warning; TFR log-order rule cross-referenced into jnwb-tfr/jnwb-visualization; CV/permutation-grouping rule cross-referenced into jnwb-statistics/jnwb-jrsa; a pointer to the 11 invalid-CV scripts so the new skill's model ladder doesn't treat one as a template. The .claude/-gitignore and skill-tree-drift findings should be resolved as part of or immediately after this patch so the patch itself stays reviewable.
verdict.SAFE_TO_RUN_STRUCTURED_DECODING_reasons: Leakage-safe flat baseline has not been run to completion (no outputs exist yet to compare a structured model against); confound-decomposition variables not materialized; deconfound script's permutation null has a real, uncharacterized asymmetry; retracted census numbers are still live in executable/imported code; no falsification-control infrastructure exists yet to distinguish nonlinearity-helped from structure-helped. Matches Sol's own explicit 'do not start structured decoding yet' -- this audit found concrete, additional, code-level reasons that instruction is correct.

falsifier: This audit is closed/superseded when: (1) the P0 items are each either fixed with a receipt or explicitly re-triaged with a documented reason for deferral; (2) Handout 2's agent/skill patch lands and is itself verified against this audit's specific conditions; (3) SAFE_TO_RUN_STRUCTURED_DECODING is re-evaluated after the leakage-safe corpus-scale run completes and the confound-decomposition variables are materialized -- at that point this node's verdict should be re-issued, not assumed to still hold.
